name: vsyncHandler
text: - Why 0.5 fps: the vsync callback 0x100268 kicks the frame's DMA, and the runtime processes VIF1 -> VU1 -> GS synchronously on the game thread. Nearly all of that time is GSCpuBackend::DrawTriangle/SampleTexture: ~2.3 s of CPU per level frame (`ps2xGsReplay traces/level2.gsr` takes 4.6 s user for 2 frames, ~23k triangles each). The game's frame limiter (D_0023FD80 = 20 fps in the level) then waits on vsyncs that only arrive between those frames.

name: setupDisplayBuffers
text: Seen: with camera+0x424 written to the 4:3 value (0.909 at 0x559A14 and 0x559EA4, the two cameras, and [address]) xemu frames the Ape as the port's PS2 camera does (`cam-rest-3way.png`: Xbox widescreen | Xbox 4:3 | port PS2).

name: setupDisplayBuffers
text: The difference is the projection (0xC4005 -> 0x1003C2): vertical FOV = FOV / A, A = (640/480) x camera+0x424 = (10/11) / K, K 0.75, or 0.5625 when the console is set to widescreen; that is FOV x 1.1 / aspect: 61.9 degrees at 4:3, 46.4 at 16:9 (PS2: 0.75 x tan(75/2) vertically at every aspect, and the port's widescreen widens the sides). The reference console's EEPROM (the copied user files) has video flags 0x90000: widescreen and 480p. So the xemu reference shots were 16:9 pictures saved at 640x480, the skater 1.34x as tall, which the 3/4 follow distance imitated.

name: updateFrustum
text: - **A callee's f0 handed on** (int_f0 widened, `readable_draft.py`): FUN_00136DA0 (tanf of an angle; Ghidra: void) returned tanf's v0, and `callGuestFunction` puts the context back after each call, so its callers (FUN_00101680, camera.cpp's `kAngleTan`) divided by their own stale f0. A function whose f0 at a return is a call's or a tail call's, and whose callers read f0 after the call, now returns `ee::Float`.

name: updateFrustum

name: scaleClutColours

text: **22 more swept engine functions written by hand, out of the sweep manifest, Verified: the pose update (kUpdatePose's group), the text draw and the animation update, 3.3% of the live-play self time ([workshop file], merged.csv); and vif1Interrupt (1.7%) marks the original's entry blocks.** Every one identical with its EE cycles on every recorded call; on by default, the game's state unchanged.

name: vif1Interrupt
text: - **Not ported, why**: the VIF1 handler FUN_001085B0 reads and writes I/O registers (D1/D2 CHCR, VIF1 STAT, an `ei`), and the recorder does not keep calls that touch I/O registers, so it cannot be checked yet (the recorder would need to keep those accesses' values). sceDmaSend (0x20EFA8, 3,600 calls a minute, 424-459 ms of the minute's EE self time, about 8 %) is an HLE stub: its time is the runtime walking the VIF1 chain (with VU1 skipped in the profile), not game code; a runtime performance task.

name: vif1Interrupt
text: - **Safe points**: every one of the 22 marks the original's entry blocks (`ee::block`) and branches back (`ee::loopBack`) as readable_draft.py's drafts do (measureText's walk is a small state machine with a step per entry block: its gotos cross three loops); vif1Interrupt (1.7% of the live-play self time) has its 21 entry blocks and 3 branches back now, in its helpers (uploadMaterial, waitForGif) where the hand-written code inlines them.

name: vif1Interrupt
text: The texture cache's level allocator FUN_00107C88, called from the VIF1 handler FUN_001085B0 when it gives a level a GS address and patches TEX0/MIPTBP1, is wrapped: each allocation reaches the renderer in stream order (`GSTextureObjectNote` through `PS2Memory::postGsSideband` and `GS::noteTextureObjects`), keyed by the object's level 0 as held in RAM (size plus FNV-1a of the indices, the pack's key). The GPU renderer binds the picture by TBP0, or by MIPTBP1 for distant models with only levels 1 and up, without decoding GS memory, and only for a texture of the picture's name (a run-time "Procedural:0" texture collided with "invisible" and blanked the juice bar).

name: vif1Interrupt
text: - **The VIF1 handler** (FUN_001085B0, `zge/render/texture_upload.cpp`): the texture request's MARK 1 block (VIF1 MARK; the next queued node's materials, VIF1 CODE's low bits the first level: 1 for the far levels) or MARK 2 (the primitive API's textures, FUN_00106258): for each material's texture with uploads pending (GsTexture +4), its CLUT and levels are placed in the GS cache if they have no address and called from a GIF packet (libgifpk in the handler's frame, the other of two buffers), which goes out on the GIF channel (D2: QWC 0, TADR, CHCR 0x145) once D2 and the GIF are idle (a poll that gives up after 2^32 reads); then VIF1 FBRST STC and EI. As the original, the level walk moves on only after a level that was uploaded, so it stops looking past the first level with nothing pending.

name: vif1Interrupt
text: - I/O registers through `ee::io` (constant addresses, and a base every path sets to one constant, as vif1Interrupt's 0x10000000 across its loop); constant scratchpad addresses too (generated code calls the runtime for them, and the recorder logs them as I/O); `--io-dynamic` (the sweep's for the hardware-facing SDK modules, and for a function whose check failed on I/O or touched a low address) decides each access through a pointer at run time (`ee::io::loadAny` / `storeAny`); an I/O load is ordered like a store. EI and DI (`ee::io::enableInterrupts`, `disableInterrupts`).

name: vif1Interrupt
text: 3,106 of 3,106 recorded calls on nine routes identical, I/O accesses and EE cycles included; the first Tutorial recording took every path but the give-up (143 uploads, 786 MARK 2 calls, 32 CLUTs and 35 levels placed).

name: vif1Interrupt
text: - **The texture request** (FUN_00108FA8): the draw list (0x27A9B0) keeps a marker, a VIF NOP in the mesh packet after the last request. A node whose materials have not asked for their textures in the cache's current generation (0x2732FC, against MaterialTable::textureEpoch) gets that NOP's interrupt bit set (bit 0 too when it is further than 30 units: its far levels only) and goes on the draw list's queue (+0x6C); the VIF1 interrupt (FUN_001085B0) then uploads the queued node's levels. Every request ends with a new marker (MARK 1, the NOP, FLUSHA, MARK 0, the last the original's tail call).

name: vif1Interrupt

name: vif1Interrupt
text: Turning the camera more than 20 degrees in a frame flushes the game's GS texture cache. Its VIF1 interrupt handler (FUN_001085B0) then assigns new GS addresses and patches TEX0 into the material blocks that the rest of the mesh chain points to. The runtime copied the whole VIF1 chain when the DMA started, so every draw after the interrupt used the previous frame's texture addresses: wrong textures on the skater, walls and HUD during fast turns. VIF1 DMA is now read as VIF1 consumes it (`DmaSource`, `fetchVif1Stream`): chain tags and data behind an interrupt-bit VIFcode are read only after STC, as on hardware, in chain and normal mode, with or without the VIF1 worker.

name: chunkEntries
text: - **The size** (`packet_size.h`, header-only, shared with the packaging tool): the builders' layout read from their code. Groups go in chunks of at most 60 entries (FUN_00108E70; whole triangles for a list); a chunk is a 24-byte unpack header, three streams with their VIF codes (16 + 8 + 16 bytes) and 24 bytes an entry for rigid and terrain parts, 28 for skinned ones, MSCAL or MSCNT, padded to a quadword; a material change pads and opens a RET tag (8 bytes). name: requestTextures
text: - **The texture request** (FUN_00108FA8): the draw list (0x27A9B0) keeps a marker, a VIF NOP in the mesh packet after the last request. A node whose materials have not asked for their textures in the cache's current generation (0x2732FC, against MaterialTable::textureEpoch) gets that NOP's interrupt bit set (bit 0 too when it is further than 30 units: its far levels only) and goes on the draw list's queue (+0x6C); the VIF1 interrupt (FUN_001085B0) then uploads the queued node's levels. name: drawRigid

What stays is the panorama's own pixels, seen from inside and below the horizon (the mirrored half), fogged (the dark panel: the fog colour where its near faces are drawn), and the skater only where the Z test happens to pass.

name: drawScene
text: ZGE2 drawScene (DM2 0x121188, 41 words) is drawSceneBySector: a 'SCENE' profile bar (newProfileBar(0, 0, 0x2555F0 the white colour word, 0x2555F8 'SCENE'), its handle at 0x25B900, start before and stop after the draw), the world's frame stamp (+0x44) up by one, resetDrawBuckets (0x108CA8: the seven buckets' end word set to their begin word, no hook), markRegionsOutOfView(cachedMatrix(g_currentCamera, 1)->translation) stored in the world's +0x40 (the area the camera is in), updateMovedNodes, drawSky, forEachWorldSector(0x121118, 0) and drawQueuedNodes; always 1. No g_sceneDrawOff test and no first-frame forEachWorldMesh. The visitor 0x121118 (drawSectorNodes): sectorInView(sector), bit 0 set returns 1, else forEachSectorNode(sector, 0x120F78, 0) (it tests bits 1-2 next and makes the same call either way) and returns 1. 0x120F78 (drawListedNode) is ZGE3's inlined listed-node draw as a function: shown bit (flags bit 32), the view stamp at node +0x170 against the world's +0x44, regionInView (0x1272D8, a function) with world +0x40 and node +0x110, nodeVisibleInView, 0x123E30, matrixMultiply (0x1128D8) of node +0x80 into +0x1C0 with cachedMatrix(camera, 0), frameLevelForDistance(node +0x15C, node +0x1C0, &level), the level against drawFlags (+0x160) bits 8-11 and setTreeLevelOfDetail, the draw check at +0x184 with +0x1B0, then 0x108CE0(node, -1, cullFlags).

name: drawScene
text: - Cause: objects whose box crosses the near plane get cull flags 0xA (0x10F6D0) and their renderer picks the clipping microprogram (type 32, 0x10B520: MSCAL 0x22 instead of 0x20, `B 0x2520`, handler 0x522). For the big ground meshes under the camera (spheres of radius 20 at y = 0, e.g. 0x70B360/0x70AD30) that program runs for more than 2 x 65536 VU1 cycles. The runtime ran each MSCAL/MSCNT with a 65536-cycle budget: the clipper stopped mid-batch, the game's next MSCNT resumed it (another 65536 cycles, still not done) and the next MSCAL started a new program over it, so most of the chunk was never kicked.

First at call #0: sp-0xb0 (EE 0x01effe40) holds 0x00230000 where the original leaves 0x00000000 (byte 2, which the original writes in the call), read by forEachSelectionCellInBox (0x1FC3D0) at its call #0, vsync 1592; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: bindSoundRpc
text: **What the game sent to the IOP.** Every sound command goes through ps2Chan.c's one RPC function 0x111C70(fn, send, size, wantReply) to Z-Axis' ZAUDIO.IRX (SID 0x47, bound in the loop 0x111BE8).

name: bindSoundRpc
text: The thread, per tick: KOFF read back, queued stream commands, stream fades and 64 KB ring refills (two 0x8000-byte halves per channel, stereo interleaved in 0x800-byte pieces), stream status {state, 2, sectors read, total} by SIF DMA to the EE object + 0x30, then one status byte per channel (4 envelope running, 1 silent; 3/2 if keyed off since the last tick) to the Init address 0x27B930.

name: bindSoundRpc
text: ZAUDIO was decompiled (headless Ghidra on the IRX's text at base 0, imports named from its stub table) for the semantics: fn 0 Init {enable, status address} / 1 Reset; 2 Alloc(size) -> sample handle (IOP pointer into a 128-entry table), 3 Free, 4 Load (handle, offset, 1 KB of PS-ADPCM); 5 ChanSetParam {channel, flags 1 SSA / 2 pitch (44.1 kHz units, sent to the SPU2 as p * 44100 / 48000) / 4 VOLL|VOLR / 8 ADSR1|ADSR2}; 6 KON / 7 KOFF (40-bit channel masks; channels 0-23 core 0 voices, 24-39 core 1 voices 0-15); 8 StrmAlloc {flags 2 stereo / 4 no source / 8 file bytes, pitch, EE object, status address} -> one of 4 streams on core 1 voices 16-23; 9 StrmFree; 10 SetParam {flags 1 pitch, 2 loop count, 4 source (path, offset, length: whole disc sectors from the one holding the offset), 8 volume, 0x10 fade}, 11 Play, 12 Stop, 13 Pause/resume, all four queued for ZAUDIO's 60 Hz IOP thread; 14/15 status writes off/on (around PSS movies).

text: BMX XXX's ZAUDIO.IRX (119,779 bytes, with .symtab and .mdebug: an unoptimised build) is AI's driver with three differences, from both decompiled: 256 sample entries (AI 128); Alloc replies {handle, SPU address} and ChanSetParam (fn 5) takes the SPU address to play from where AI's takes the sample handle (SSA = *(handle+8)), so BMX's EE starts each sound at its offset in a bank allocation; at a fade's end flag 4 sets state 8 and flag 2 alone state 6 (AI's: flag 2 sets 8).

name: iopCommand

Now an argument register the callee returned with unchanged holds the readable's passed value, else what the last call left (the caller's registers before the first call).

Found by cov5's differential cases (BMX, a null host path word: 14 of 175 differed); fixed in cov5's dded27ea1: the loaders return whether every module loaded and give the failing name apart. After the fix the 175 cases are identical, and the corpus replays (AI 19, DM2 66, BMX 33 files), lc 21/21 and dm2logic 6/6 pass.

name: ps2SifInit
text: BMX XXX's angleSin (0x117340) and angleCos (0x117360) start VU0 microprogram 0 (VCALLMS 0, the program loadVu0Microprogram uploads from vu0MicroprogramChain 0x2444A0, 29 pairs): radians = angle * 2pi/65536; x = radians - pi/2, y = radians; each lane's cosine by the turn's fraction (1.5*2^23 bias), u = |f - 1/2| - 1/4 and an odd polynomial for sin(2 pi u) to u^9. x is the sine (angleSin), y the cosine (angleCos); max error against sin/cos 7.5e-7. No other BMX function starts a VU0 microprogram; the GameCube build calls sinf, the Xbox x87. Readable: zge/math/angle.cpp cosineOnVu0, sineAndCosineOnVu0 (own bodies sineFromVu0, cosineFromVu0).

name: ps2SifInit
text: BMX XXX angleSin's VU0 microprogram (vu0MicroprogramChain, VCALLMS 0) runs on all four lanes of vf1 as QMTC2 handed it: x the angle, z and w the low word of a0's upper half (whatever the last 128-bit move through a0 left: string bytes, pointers, 0 in the recordings). It leaves vf1 the cosines (x sine, y cosine), vf2 u^8, vf3 u^4, vf4 u*39.71, vf5 u*81.60, vf6 u^3*-76.57, ACC the sum before the u^9 term, VI15 4, I 6.2831850 and its MAC/status flags; later vector code reads them (the scale macro's VMULx.xyz vf6 then SQC2 vf6 stores vf6.w into game memory, 0x10ed78's SQC2 vf2 stores vf2.w).

name: ps2SifInit
text: The readable's model of the microprogram (zge/math/angle.cpp with ee::vu0::MicroLane: the VU interpreter's operand and result clamping, flags from the exact double) matched all 18,862 recorded calls' vf1-vf6, ACC, MAC and status, and the runtime's VU1Interpreter itself on 2,131,072 runs (all 65536 angles, random upper halves incl. exponent 254/255 and denormals, random prior state): 0 differ.

name: ps2SifInit
text: ps2xFnCheck cannot judge BMX XXX's angleSin/angleCos (0x117340, 0x117360): its VU0 code memory is empty, so the original's VCALLMS 0 runs nothing and every recorded call is original_bad (r8 left as the angle), the readable skipped. Checked instead offline (portbmx2 tools/angle_rec.py): all 98 recordings, 9431 calls each, the recorded f0 bit-identical to the readable maths; and all 65536 angles against the ELF's microcode on a sequential VU model. A checker that loads BMX's VU0 microprogram before replaying would judge them.

name: ps2SifInit
text: The runtime's VU interpreter clamps a micro-mode result past FLT_MAX (and an exponent-255 operand) to 0x7F7FFFFF, where the macro-mode helpers (ps2_vmul etc.) give 0x7FFFFFFF: 2174 of the recorded calls overflow in z/w (u^2 of string-byte inputs), so a readable model of a VCALLMS must use the micro-mode rule (ee::vu0::MicroLane), not ee::vu0::mul.

name: pollPads
text: - **The pad's pressed word is not a bug.** The engine's pad update (FUN_00118ED0, the tail of 0x14C680, called only from updatePads) stores the device's +0x0C as this read's buttons XOR the last read's: the buttons that changed (down or up), +0x10 the released ones, +0x08 the held ones; updatePads copies +0x0C into PadState.pressed. Measured with PS2X_CONTROL (`hold CROSS 20`, `down` / `up CIRCLE`, `hold L1+R1 20`): held 0x80 at ticks 1502-1521, pressed 0x80 at 1502 and again at 1522 (the release), 0 between; L1+R1 0x300 the same. A press is one frame; cov-controls' recorder has to catch that frame (skater.h's "pressed: this frame" means changed this frame).

Uncovered: 0x1196A4, 0x119704, 0x11973C are alignment nops no branch reaches (loop heads follow them); 0x1196D8 (demux loop left because the movie ended: a skip while demuxing), 0x1196E0 (videoDecFlush not yet flushing), 0x119730 (the isFlushed wait left: flushed, or ended), 0x119740 0x119768 0x119760 (the wait while the movie stays ended, keepsRunning set), 0x11974C 0x119750 (keepsRunning cleared by endMovie: parked set, the park loop), 0x119778 (the movie left the ended state: start over). Why not recorded: the frame rule stops at the first wait of a vsync, and in AI the park's wait always shares its vsync with an earlier demux wait (START at 9 to 28 tried); a played movie's flush wait runs ~65k lone polls a vsync (~300 MB of record a vsync) for hundreds of vsyncs. Stays Draft.

name: movieDefaultMain
text: - **AKA logo movie ran at 24 vsyncs/s** (then the old pacer caught up at 402): the game's CD stream thread (func_00119680) polls with RotateThreadReadyQueue, and each pass cost the EE thread far more than its EE cycles. Two runtime costs, both fixed: the kernel snapshot was rebuilt (allocations, sorts) on every kernel call, now lazily at idle, VBlank and every 4096 dispatches (abc5e88, 24 -> 31); the IOP ran its whole service pass for every IOP cycle the EE advanced, now it only moves the clock while no IOP thread is ready and nothing is due (01a6de2, -> 60; off while an SPU2 DMA runs, so results are the same: `logiccheck.py run polish-logic` all 21 checkpoints MATCH).

name: movieDefaultMain
text: PS2X_MOVIES=hle stalled for good at PS2X_EE_SCALE=4096 (AI vsync 48, DM2 vsync 251, playbot's clock): movieDefaultMain polls through switchThread = RotateThreadReadyQueue while it is the only ready thread at priority 10, and each pass charged 1/4096 of its cycles (~1e8 passes to the next vblank). Not audio, not pacing: at clock 1, unpaced and muted, the boot reached the menu (2685). Fixed in EeScheduler::rotateReadyQueue (movies2): at K > 1 a lone yield's pass is charged at the PS2's clock. A recording of it needs PS2X_FNREC_ATOMIC=0: with safe points held off the never-returning thread spins alone for good.

name: checkDvdResult
text: - **An argument the readable function leaves out is not checked (for the readable agent).** ps2xFnCheck compares the argument registers of each callee call up to the count the readable function passed (`regs.intCount`), so a callee argument the port omits passes every replay. DM2's engine query 0x11B4A8 takes its hit list in t2, which the original sets in its prologue apart from the other arguments; the port passed six, all replays were identical, and in DM2 the queries found nothing (dm2logic 2/6, the rider at the origin). Comparing a callee's recorded a0-t3 that the readable leaves unset (where the original's callee reads them) would catch it.

name: endSaveJob
text: A memory card job never returns (endMemoryCardJob deletes its thread), so the recorder keeps none. PS2X_JOB_RETURNS=1 with PS2X_READABLE=0x11D230 makes it return (not at 0x11D82C, whose code after the call never runs in the game and would loop), and the job's call comes to its end. name: boxFaceTree
text: boxFaceTree tests a face only on the box's own three axes (its matrix's rows): the nine edge-cross axes (box axis x face edge) are worked out only when the axis already in their slot (g_queryEdgeAxes, the query state's last 0x90 bytes) is longer than 1e-10, and initQueries clears those slots, so the game never works one out and never tests one; the face's normal is never an axis either. name: collisionQuery
text: So a route can try calls for as long as it plays and keeps only new paths: the per-vsync cap counts calls recorded (kept or not), spread over the vsync's calls (every n-th from a random phase, n from the count the vsync before made: the frame's other callers, not its first ones), with no stride. A call that ran nothing new is dropped; every 16 such in a row double the function's rest (vsyncs it is not recorded, at most 120), and a vsync without a call of it (a state's callback between moves, a move's code) ends the rest, so each episode is recorded from its start.

name: collisionQuery
text: - **A query** (SphereQuery, built in FUN_00125BE0's frame): kind, shape (sphere {centre, radius}, segment {start, end}, box, swept box), flags (4: hit points in world space, 8 / 0x10: skip / keep listed nodes, 0x20: refresh a cache, 0x40: the cache's own limits, 0x80: all faces, 0x1C00: debug draw), a filter callback and its context, the caller's results and node list, the bounds, the hit being tested, the stamp. Results (0x296EC8, copied to the caller's): a count and HitNodes {node, part, face count, FaceHits}; a FaceHit (0x30 bytes): face index, point (+0x10), distance (+0x20). Segments keep only the nearest face; spheres every face they touch.

name: collisionQuery

The original builds the buffer's descriptor in a3 and the flags word in t0 (the masks 3 and -16 in t1, t2), and FUN_00135768 and memcpy leave them for FUN_00103230: the readable version passes them to those calls as the original has them and hands on what the callees leave.

name: loadMaterial
text: **Cause: the materials' surface sound, numbered differently in the two games and copied as it was.** Every material carries an 8-byte tag record that both games' loaders copy from the MATI chunk (AI FUN_00128A98 from +0x1C, DM2 FUN_0011CE38 from +0x18)

name: loadMaterial
text: *The surface sound, numbered differently in the two games and copied as it was.* Every material's 8-byte tag record (AI MATI +0x1C, DM2 +0x18; AI FUN_00128A98, DM2 FUN_0011CE38) starts with the surface sound (the table in "DM2 levels: You went swimming!").

name: loadMaterial
text: The surface sound is read from RAM: the material's one-record tag table (material + 0x10, filled at load from MATI +0x1C by FUN_00128A98) has no host mirror; the engine's collision host data covers the parts' TGFT / TGFE tables only.

name: loadMaterial
text: Material +0x10 is a one-record tag table (makeBuffer: type 6, descriptor 0x4083, always: the original's bit-field writes over the frame word end in 0x4083 with the upper word 0) whose record is Material +0x20, copied from MATI +0x1C (tagRecord, the surface sound first).

name: loadMaterial
text: Verdicts (ps2xFnCheck `--cycles`, this round's base build against the final one, the same corpus clone): 59,601 files the same, 64 better (fn_128A98 fails -> passes, 32 files: gamehand4's Verified version merged; 0x187C90 newly readable, 32), none worse.

name: loadMaterial
text: The readable loadMaterial writes the descriptor's high word through a uint32_t* (frame +0x04) between two writes through the uint64_t& descriptorWord; strict aliasing lets the compiler keep the stale high word, which makeBuffer copies to Material +0x18. The original's sw zero,4(sp) makes it 0 whatever the stack held. Plain runs pass only because that stack word is 0; under career_ab.py stale's stores fill on (b) has 0x5A5A5A5A in every material. One store, (descriptor & 0xFFFFFFF0) | 3, matches off under the fill (stalegate4/loadMaterial-fix.patch).

name: materialHasAlpha
text: Material flags bit 34 is the first texture's flag bit 0 (updateMaterialAlphaFlag, read by materialHasAlpha), bit 35 kMaterialFlagBlended (materialIsBlended, was materialIsSecondClass), bit 39 MATI bit 10 (materialFlagBit39, was materialTableBit39: a material's bit, not a table's): refreshMaterialTableFlags leaves such materials out of the table's kMaterialTableBlended (texture alpha, 0x10000) and kMaterialTableSecondClass (blended, 0x20000).

name: materialHasAlpha
text: DM2's counterpart is 0x0011D730, not 0x0011D740: DM2's refreshMaterialTableFlags calls 0x11D730 first (its result sets the table's texture-alpha flag, bit 0 there) and 0x11D740 second (the blended flag, bit 1); 0x11D730 reads material flag bit 33, which DM2's updateMaterialAlphaFlag (0x11D098) sets from the texture's alpha byte. ZGE2's material flag bits sit one lower than ZGE3's (33 texture alpha, 34 blended).

name: materialIsBlended
text: DM2's counterpart is 0x0011D740 (reads material flag bit 34, ZGE2's blended bit: the second call of DM2's refreshMaterialTableFlags, whose result sets the table's second-class flag), not 0x0011D720 (bit 35).

name: materialFlagBit39
text: DM2 has no counterpart: ZGE2 has no leave-out bit 39 (DM2's loadMaterial sets no flag from the MATI, its refreshMaterialTableFlags skips no material). The pair with 0x0011D730 is positional; 0x11D730 is DM2's materialHasAlpha.

First at call #0: sp-0xb8 (EE 0x01eff628) holds 0x73696854 where the original leaves 0x00000011 (byte 1, which the original writes in the call), read by loadBoneChunk (0x130968) at its call #0, vsync 1202 (order within the vsync not recorded); perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: addToCells
text: - Hang on the tutorial's LOADING screen: the collision grid loop at 0x12E01C (func_0012DED8) spun ~2^31 times on an object whose bounding box was +-5e19. Chain: matrix-to-quaternion 0x14D130 uses `sqrt.s $f4, $f4` (0x46040104). The R5900 reads SQRT.S's operand from ft; the translator used fs ($f0), so the quaternion got a -max component, quat-to-matrix 0x14D030 produced a +-5e19 rotation, and every child transform inherited it. Fixed in PS2Recomp 6b4c201 (test added). Found with PS2X_WATCH32 on the object's matrix and quaternion words plus PS2X_TRACE_CALLS on the setters.

name: readTehdChunk
text: A level's ZIT is FSCN { TERR { TEHD, ZFTX, ZFGE, ZFIS, ZFSD } }: TEHD is 0x30 bytes, cell size (50, 50, 50 in every stock level), the world box's low and high corners, and the grid counts per axis ((high - low) / cell: the Movie Lot 20 x 8 x 17, the Tutorial 14 x 4 x 13); readTehdChunk reads only the first 0x24 bytes and makes the collision world from them. The ZF* chunks name the level's TXR, GEO, INS and DAT files, read from the ZIT's own folder (includeChunkFile). The ZIT holds no geometry: a new level's is these names and a box that holds its collidable instances.

name: readTehdChunk
text: TEHD is 0x30 bytes on disc (cell size, box low, box high as float3 each, then three u32 cell counts = (high - low) / cell); readTehdChunk reads the first 0x24 only, so the counts are the exporter's and nothing reads them. A level made by ai_level_convert.py writes them anyway.

name: loadCollisionTreeChunk
text: TGCI on disc: {u32 part id, u32 bytes, tree}, the tree's split nodes and leaves in preorder (8 bytes each), then every leaf's u16 face list in the same order (an empty leaf points at where the next list starts), the chunk padded to 4 bytes with zeros. Byte +1 of every node is unread (checkFaceTree and the queries read +0, +2, +4, +6) and holds varying leftovers in 4,987 of the 6,505 stock trees; a writer puts 0 there. ai_level_write.py CollisionTree reads and writes the layout byte-identically on all 21 level folders.

name: loadCollisionTreeChunk
text: The tree, not the face flag, decides what is solid on an object with a TGCI: across the 21 AI level folders the 6,505 stock trees list no face without 0x2000, but 478 of them leave out 1,038 valid faces that have it (the Tutorial 17 faces in 17 trees), and 9,165 faces with 0x2000 have a vertex index past the part's vertex count (never in a tree). A tree rebuilt over every 0x2000 face (ai_level_write.py rewrite --variant-all-faces) ran logiccheck's Tutorial route the same to ref16 and diverged at ref17-manual-done (16.7 m); 1,903 objects have no tree and AI's query takes all their 0x2000 faces (214,745).

name: newBuffer
text: A part's face tags (TGFT) and face edges (TGFE) are tag tables (FUN_001356D8 makes one: a 16-byte header with type 6, a reference count, the descriptor, the index count and the heap; the indices; the records at the next 16 bytes). The game reads and writes the records only through the engine's accessors, and holds record addresses in the RAM table.

name: releaseTagTable
text: A mirror goes when releaseTagTable frees its table, or when a new table is noted over it. tagWord on a mirror charges memcpy's two dispatches (16 cycles) and writes the word to the frame, as the original's memcpy does.

name: makeBuffer
text: - **loadMaterial** (FUN_00128A98, from the engine's sweep): the sweep's draft failed after drafter16's argument fix (0x103230 reads a3 and t0, which the draft never set). The original builds the buffer's descriptor in a3 and the flags word in t0 (the masks 3 and -16 in t1, t2), and FUN_00135768 and memcpy leave them for FUN_00103230: the readable version passes them to those calls as the original has them and hands on what the callees leave.

name: heapTake
text: **1. An idle EE waits for the IOP, not the vblank** (generic). With every EE thread waiting, `EeScheduler::waitForEvent` advanced the clock to the next EE event (the vblank) in one step, so whatever the IOP sent back (ZCDDVD's completion RPC on SID 0x46, other replies, SIF commands) was seen once per vsync. The IOP now reports when it next runs guest code (`IopSubsystem::eeCyclesUntilWork`: a ready thread, a delay ending, a DMA interrupt, a callback, a timer, SPU2 interrupts while a DMA runs; plain mixing ticks do not count) and the idle EE advances only to that point (at least 4096 EE cycles, about a SIF round trip) and looks again. Host pacing still happens at the vblank.

name: loadStringTableFile

name: stringTableText
text: 1. **A symbol per address.** Every address the readable code uses gets a name in one committed header, `game/symbols.h`: `READABLE_SYMBOL(stringTableText, Function, 0x00148408)`, `READABLE_SYMBOL(g_stringTable, Global, 0x00273B40)`, the AI address being the key it has always been. A tool (readable_symbols.py) lists the literals left in the folder; the first step is mechanical and changes nothing in AI: literals become `sym::name`, `ee::Global<T, 0x...>` becomes `ee::Global<T, sym::g_stringTable>`, `ee::call<R>(0x...)` becomes `ee::call<R>(sym::...)`, READABLE_FUNCTION takes the symbol (`READABLE_FUNCTION(sym::stringTableText, stringTableText, Tested)`).

name: stringTableText
text: - **`PS2X_FNREC=@file`** (one function a line, `#` comments, each line optionally with its own caps: `0x00148408 200 8`); a small cap doubles its stride after an eighth of it; at most 64 recording files open at once (Windows' C runtime allows 512).

name: stringTableText
text: What ties the readable code to AI today: the registration's address (`READABLE_FUNCTION(0x00148408, stringTableText, Tested)`), `ee::Global<T, 0x00273B40>` (282 uses), `ee::call<R>(address)` with an address literal or a `k...` constant (about 560 distinct 0x001xxxxx/0x002xxxxx literals in the folder), `game::call<&fn>` (323, resolved through the registration: fine once registrations are per game), and struct layouts (`static_assert` on offsets).

name: nameHash

name: nameHash

name: nameHash
text: BMX XXX's nameHash (0x143B18) is identical to AI's and replays identical (Tested), but build_table's settle_votes demotes it to entry: its lui 0x24 + addiu 8 is the lowercase table's base with -'a' folded in (AI table 0x23FFA7, BMX [address]), which collides numerically with the global at AI 0x240008 that renderCountedFrame and the collision code read (BMX [address]). A data vote of a folded, indexed base is not the symbol at that address.

name: nameHash
text: The bind table's demotion of BMX's nameHash (0x143B18) was the table builder's: walk_pair kept a %hi in v0 across a jal, so 0x17E0A0's and 0x1686C8's move s0, v0; sb/sh zero, 8(s0) voted AI 0x240008 (g_upperCaseLetters, A..Z in both ELFs; BMX [address]) to BMX [address]. Fixed in readable_symbols.py (a call's caller-saved registers hold no %hi past its delay slot): nameHash and findObjects are body (level 2) again.

name: readPads
text: - **The pad's pressed word is not a bug.** The engine's pad update (FUN_00118ED0, the tail of 0x14C680, called only from updatePads) stores the device's +0x0C as this read's buttons XOR the last read's: the buttons that changed (down or up), +0x10 the released ones, +0x08 the held ones; updatePads copies +0x0C into PadState.pressed. Measured with PS2X_CONTROL (`hold CROSS 20`, `down` / `up CIRCLE`, `hold L1+R1 20`): held 0x80 at ticks 1502-1521, pressed 0x80 at 1502 and again at 1522 (the release), 0 between; L1+R1 0x300 the same. A press is one frame; cov-controls' recorder has to catch that frame (skater.h's "pressed: this frame" means changed this frame).

name: quaternionToMatrix
text: - Hang on the tutorial's LOADING screen: the collision grid loop at 0x12E01C (func_0012DED8) spun ~2^31 times on an object whose bounding box was +-5e19. Chain: matrix-to-quaternion 0x14D130 uses `sqrt.s $f4, $f4` (0x46040104). The R5900 reads SQRT.S's operand from ft; the translator used fs ($f0), so the quaternion got a -max component, quat-to-matrix 0x14D030 produced a +-5e19 rotation, and every child transform inherited it. Fixed in PS2Recomp 6b4c201 (test added). Found with PS2X_WATCH32 on the object's matrix and quaternion words plus PS2X_TRACE_CALLS on the setters.

text: - **VU0**: zge/math/vu0_ops.h runs the FMAC chains (VMULA / VMADDA / VMADD by a lane, VMUL, VADDbc, VMINI / VMAX, VDIV, VMULq) on the context's registers with the generated code's flags, so matrixMultiply and matrixInvertRigid (READABLE_FUNCTION_VU0) leave VU0 as the originals do (matrixInvertRigid's T.w is vf9's previous w, boxTransform's corners carry it too); its scratch registers are thread-local (ee::vu0::Machine zeroes a 1.6 KB context each time one is made, measurable in hot routines: see below).

name: updatePose
text: New layouts: zge/scene/scene.h (Scene: flags with kSceneScaled, kSceneKeysChanged, kSceneSkinned at bits 32-34, position, scale, orientation, bones, the animator, a skinned model's node; SceneBone 0x40 bytes: node, key, matrices, bind position, child / sibling / parent; BoneKey; BoneMatrices, laid out as a node's local and world so that a rigid model's bones point into their nodes; SceneObject: kObjectPoseStale = bit 7, set by markPoseStale and cleared by updatePose), zge/scene/animation.h (Animator, AnimationChannel 0x90 bytes with its weighted sums, AnimationTrack with its fades and key cursors, RotationKey in 1/16384 and key times in 1/128, AnimationEvent), zge/text/font.h (Font, moved from utilities.cpp: height, pages, glyphs; FontPage 0x28 bytes; Glyph; TextStyle, the engine's view of zgui's: scale, colour, alignment nibbles, line and letter spacing, monospaced, angle, measured size).

name: setCameraObjectOrientation
text: setCameraObjectOrientation's matrix is on its stack and quaternionToMatrix writes no w lane, so each row's w is the stack's residue; setCameraMatrix copies it to the camera and beginViewDraws sends forward's w (Camera +0xDC) to VU1 at 0x3F3. That word (off 1.0, defaults 0 or -7.6e-6) is career_ab.py's vif1 difference on the career input, ticks 1258 to 3160 (660 vsyncs, the same before zgehand17); gif stream equal, but the A/B runs PS2X_VU1_SKIP. Main stack residue, not a game logic difference.

name: sourceHeard
text: - **AI's and DM2's ZSD banks differ in one record.** The sample record (header +0x10 / +0x14) is 0x14 bytes in DM2 and 0x18 in AI: AI inserts +6, a distance scale (FUN_0016FAE0: the listener hears it within sqrt(80^2 x 0x240810[b]); DM2's range is a fixed 40); the rest of the bank (wave references, the wave table, PS-ADPCM) is the same. `ps2xRuntime/tools/dm2_sound.py` makes DM2's rider samples into AI's layout at build time; AI's own loader FUN_00112FD8 takes the result (served through a game-files provider as ASSETS/AUDIO/DM2/RIDER.ZSD).

name: sourceHeard
text: - **Sound emitters** (updateSoundEmitters): the level's list at gp-0x29DC (by +0x30), each frame of play (game mode 2): a repeating emitter counts down its interval and, when due, its sample is played where it stands at the volume and pan the listener hears it with (0x16FAE0, times the options' effects volume; the overrun kept for the next wait); a continuous one has its sound source moved to it and set to full level (soundEvent 50). No route's level has a repeating emitter (the three uncovered blocks). The draft passed 0x16FAE0 four arguments; the original sets a fifth (t0 = sp + 2), which the callee never reads; the readable call passes it.

name: stringSetText
text: With every default-on function traced it brackets a write to one call; it found the tick-1,117 culprit (evaluate's `sd s0, 0x40(sp)`). `PS2X_FNCYCLES_FROM` applies to the W and H lines too. `PS2X_FNCYCLES_ARGS` also writes a line for a traced function's direct call (game::call: `addr call tick cycle direct sp=<stack top> ctxsp=<context sp>`): the stack top is where the callee's frame goes, so the sp of every call compares with the original's (drafter21: the frames 0x50 to 0xA0 above the original's under stringSetText).

name: stringSetText
text: `PS2X_FNCYCLES_FROM=<tick>` writes lines only for calls from that vsync tick (every default-on function over a window of a few ticks). `PS2X_FNCYCLES_WATCH=<addr>[+<bytes>][,...]:<file>` (drafter21): a memory write-watch in the cycle tracer.

name: stringSetText
text: `PS2X_TRACE_EE=<from>:<to>:<file>` (EeScheduler, drafter23) writes every EE cycle charge (`A cycle cycles host-return-address`), checkpoint test (`C cycle cycles due`) and scheduler dispatch (`D cycle pc`) whose cycle is in [from, to] (the slide first, for atos): with two runs' `PS2X_FNCYCLES` entry cycles it shows which 8 cycles one side charges and the other does not. The recorder keeps a call that waits (`PS2X_FNREC_WAITS=0` drops it as before): the session is parked at the waiting call's return point and goes on when its thread comes back there; the summary line counts the calls parked and kept.

name: stringSetText
text: - **String's setText** (stringSetText, the String variable type's set-from-text): the value's buffer (its room ended by a 0x01 byte) given back and a new one taken when the text does not fit, then the text copied with its escapes turned: \" into " (kept as \" between quotes), \\ into \, \n into CR LF (not between quotes), CR LF kept, a lone LF into CR; each " not escaped starts or ends a quote. The buffer is read again at every byte written, as the original does.

name: stringSetText
text: A call traced with `PS2X_FNCYCLES` from a readable caller returns to the resume slot; the tracer pairs a late return with its call by ra and sp (drafter15). ps2xFnCheck's result line has `args_left` and `first_args_left` (drafter15): calls whose callee reads an argument register the readable call did not pass, with another value than the original's. `readable_sweep.py manifest-demote --promote --drafts` also registers as Tested a Draft that was never demoted (one set aside whole and checked again).

name: stringSetText
text: Each range (main RAM, or the scratchpad at 0x70000000; 16 bytes unless `+bytes`, up to 16 KB) is compared at every traced function's entry and return (table calls and game::call's direct ones) and at every vsync with what it held before; a change writes `W in|out|din|dout|vsync addr call tick cycle sp ra @range: old -> new` (`in`: seen at a traced call's entry, so written before it; `out`: at its return, by the call or its callees; a range over 32 bytes prints how many bytes changed and the 16 around the first). Every vsync writes `H tick @range fnv1a`, so two runs' files compare tick by tick (the scratchpad: state the RAM dumps leave out).

name: stringSetText
text: Run with the defaults and with a readable function on, the same call has the same entry cycle until the first difference; [workshop file] compares two such files. `PS2X_FNCYCLES_ARGS=<file>` (drafter20) writes, for each table call of a traced function, a line at its entry (address, call number, tick, entry cycle, a0 to a3, and for a0 and a1 that point into RAM the first 40 bytes there as text and the first 16 in hex, then sp and ra) and, at an in-place return, the registers (GPRs' low words, FPRs' bits): for the call whose data differs between two runs (a string function reading past a 0, a caller reading a temporary).

name: stringSetText
text: `PS2X_FNCYCLES=<addr>[,<addr>...]:<file>` (or `@<list file>:<file>`; sweepfix) wraps those function starts in the dispatch table at the first vsync and writes a line a call: address, call number, vsync tick, the EE cycle at entry, the EE cycles to the return to its caller, and how it ended (`ret`: in place; `late`: it gave the EE back to the scheduler halfway, a safe point or a suspendable function's guest call, and came back to its return address through the scheduler, whose table slot is wrapped then; `lost`).

name: stringSetText
text: `PS2X_READABLE_FRAMES=0` (drafter22; default 1) turns the frame table off: readable functions then run as before round 22 (callees `ee::kCalleeStackGap` below a table entry's sp, a function called directly in its caller's place, no register saves but the ones a function writes itself); for A/B runs of the stack residue ([workshop file]). `PS2X_READABLE_SAFEPOINTS=0` (safepoints; default 1) runs readable functions straight through as before the round: off a fiber unless `_WAITS`, no check at their own safe points. `PS2X_SAFEPOINT_TRACE=1` logs every fiber that leaves at a safe point and every resume (function, sp, thread).

name: stringSetText
text: `PS2X_TRACE_MOVIES=1` also prints the libmpeg HLE's stall lines (`[MPEG:hold]`, `[MPEG:dry]`, `[MPEG:wait]`, each the 1st, 2nd, 4th ... time). Round 12 also restored the `grindx` command, which the dispatch had lost ("unknown command grindx": the corpus' grinds route stopped there). `tools/run-game.sh`'s `STOP_TICK` reads the vsync from `[state]` and `[frame:upload]` lines only (the runner's `[run:tick]` lines count something else and could stop a run early).

text: The first is stringSetText 0x181728 (hand-written, game/aggressive/zgui/variable_types.cpp): it has no StackFrame, so its callees get their stack 0x40 below its sp (ee::kCalleeStackGap), where the original's frame is 0xA0; 0x183558 (the command that runs a statement inside another) is the same, and the offsets add up (+0x50, +0xA0) down to evaluate and the handler. Each such frame leaves its dead stack elsewhere.

name: stringSetText
text: The recorder's summary line counts the calls that waited (they unwound to the scheduler through it and are not kept). ps2xFnCheck caps itself (drafter23, after the 2026-10-26 panic): `--max-mem-mb MB` (default 2048, 0 for none) polls its own memory every 20 ms (macOS phys_footprint, as memguard.py reads it; Linux resident; Windows private bytes) and above it ends as a fault (`phase="<phase> (memory: N MB, the cap M MB)"`), whoever runs it; `--runaway K` (default 64, 0 for none) ends a replayed call (either version) that charges more than K times the EE cycles the recording says the call charged in the game, plus 2^24, as a fault at once (`(runaway: ...)`); the `--markers` order logs are bounded. fncheck_corpus.py passes `--max-mem-mb` at 0.9 times its own `--max-mem-gb` to a binary that has the option, and does not cache timeout or memory faults.

name: stringSetText
text: `ps2xFnCheck --call-timeout S` (drafter22; default 60, 0 for none): a replayed call still running after S seconds ends the process with a `[fncheck:fault]` line (phase `... (timeout)`), which fncheck_corpus.py takes as a fault and goes on after the file. `--call-blocks` writes a `[fncheck:callblocks] address= file= call= ok= blocks=` line per replayed call of the original: the blocks (hex starts) it ran. ps2xFnCheck starts COP0 Count at 0 for every replay.

name: stringSetText

name: setupCollisionPart
text: Functions a round adds are recorded into the same folders with `--only` (seconds to minutes for a handful: six functions over the whole lc input in 29 s, eight over the seven other routes in 9 minutes). Re-run cmake on the build first, since the traced originals are listed at configure time, and do not rebuild the runner while a batch records: the script says when a function was not recorded for either reason (`NOT RECORDED` in record.log and runs.json). Functions whose calls make 5,000 callee calls or more (the level set-up's nearest-edge search, 0x186BF8) are recorded on the lc route only.

name: setupCollisionPart
text: - **Tag tables** (TGFT face tags, Part +0x44; TGFE face edges, +0x4C): a 16-byte header (descriptor: index width kind, record bytes, records; the index count), an index per element (a face; three per face for edges; 0xFF/0xFFFF none), then at the next 16 bytes the records. A face tag record (28 bytes) has the surface kind at +0x0C; an edge record (24 bytes) its kind at +0x08 (1 or 9 go with kind-1 faces, 2 with kind 2). The level's setup (FUN_00186BF8, game side) fills words at load: an edge record's +0x04 (the last element that picks it), a kind-0xB face tag's +0x08 (its face), a kind 1 or 2 face tag's +0x04 (the nearest matching edge, worked out from the geometry).

name: setupCollisionPart
text: Since round 14 each route is one pass (`--passes all`, the default): the function list goes to the runner as a file (`PS2X_FNREC=@file`), each function with its own caps, light ones 200 calls at most 8 a vsync, heavy ones (an average of 8 or more callee calls a call in earlier recordings, or 10 or more call sites when never recorded) 50 at 1 a vsync; a small cap doubles its stride after an eighth of it, so the calls spread over the run. Before (a full RAM diff of about 6 ms around every callee call) each route had a light pass (`PS2X_FNREC_MAX=1000 PS2X_FNREC_PER_VSYNC=8`) and a heavy one (`100` / `1`); `--passes light,heavy` still records that way.

text: - **The rail filter** (railFilter, FUN_00187C90: searchRails' sphere query calls it for each scene object it meets; its draft did not compile, so it was Planned): over the object's grind edges (its collision part +0x4C, the TGFE records) the nearest within the context's radius the skater can get onto: of the tag asked for (tag 0 takes any edge whose byte +0x09, grindable, is set; an edge whose ends lie within 1e-5 has that byte cleared), not the double rail now ground (either way round, Grind/Walls Sloppy Vert Weld apart) nor the rail now ground, ahead of the skater or with an end at the point of the rail now ground nearest it, along the heading within the context's least |cos| (Min Grind Angle going on from a rail's end); the edge goes to the context's Rail record (its +0x08, the found flag, is the edge's collision part) and its distance becomes the radius, so the nearest wins.

name: railFilter
text: A TGFE record is one edge, not a class of edges: railFilter walks the object's records and considerEdge takes each record's own edge (edgeId, the element the load writes from the last face edge whose index picks the record), so a record shared by N face edges leaves one rail on the object. Every stock part's record count equals its tagged edge count (HANGER's 153 TGFE parts). A level writer must write one record per tagged face edge: the Deck's first build shared one record per (kind, flags, sound) and the game's rail search found 154 of 4,727 tagged edges, one per object.

name: showOverlayText
text: - **DM2 on other levels for recordings.** A fresh Free Ride opens only Woodward Camp: the level select's native bmxSetupLevelStats (0x1AFE58) locks a value (UILIB's LockLevel, the toggler disabled) unless bit 0 of the level's progress flags is set for player 1's rider. With `PS2X_DEV_UNLOCK_ALL=1` (or `PS2X_DM2_OPEN_LEVELS=1`) DM2's override sets it for every rider and level each vsync (`dave_mirra_devlevels.cpp`; recomp/DEVTOOLS.md); all eight levels then load from a fresh Free Ride (menu values 1-7 measured: the session's level ids 1, 0, 3, 6, 5, 4, 7, the level's frame counter running).

name: showOverlayText
text: In Dave Mirra BMX 2 the same setting (or `PS2X_DM2_OPEN_LEVELS=1`) opens every level in the level select (dave_mirra_devlevels.cpp, PS2Recomp `rider5`): each vsync it sets bit 0 ("open") of the progress flags of each of DM2's eight levels for every rider (0x2174B4 + rider x 0x3C8 + 0x13C + level x 0x44 + 0x3C), which bmxSetupLevelStats (0x1AFE58) reads before it locks a level. The Xbox levels' career keeps its own (dave_mirra_xcareer.cpp). Pad scripts then reach any level with RIGHT presses at the level select (menu value v: v presses; level ids by value 2, 1, 0, 3, 6, 5, 4, 7). Off by default.

name: showOverlayText
text: DM2 PS2 bmxSetupLevelStats: a level select value is locked unless progress bit 1 (+0x13C + level*0x44 + 0x3C) is set for player 1's character; Free Ride's Venice/Greenville (values 9, 10, Woodward's slot) read the Xbox level's swapped progress, so they start locked and the levels or everything cheat opens them (xcareer).

name: showOverlayText
text: BMX XXX game.c: the running turn's end for modes 0..16 (table 0x284280 by mode; 17..19 have 0x1B0140, 0x1B0470, 0x1B0D38): DM2's turn-end stages in the round's byte +0xD (riding, line begun, last line, at rest 30 frames, ended) plus stage 4 (a rider with flag byte 0 bit 0x40, or mode 18's record check in 0x1B2770, ends the turn 240 frames on, the round's byte +0x10 = a player); it sets round flags 0x80 (last line: no clock), 0x20 (at rest: tricks not scored), 0x100 (ended).

text: - **A recorder limit** (for the engine side): a recorded function that calls itself, where both calls leave by a tail call (setSkaterScore's rollover), is recorded with the inner call's tail call taking the outer one's along (the recorder runs the inner's jump on to the outer's return, through entry_001B4DFC): the recording has one call to FUN_001B0040 where the game makes two. The readable version makes both, so those two calls differ; the other 13 are identical. Checked in the game instead: not done (next steps).

name: showScore
text: A related limit: a function recorded with PS2X_FNREC is not seen when untraced generated code reaches it by a tail call (`j`, compiled to a direct C++ call that bypasses the function table): in the off run's rollover the outer's tail call to showScore was not recorded (2 calls recorded where the game made 3).

name: showScore
text: Both showScore calls and the outer's last instructions become the effects and `after` registers of the one tail-call record, and the outer's cycles after 0x1B4DFC are not counted (the record's cycles are 8 less than the readable version's per rollover call: the folded call). A fix: when the tail-pending loop reaches an address inside the recorded function itself (a resumable entry), close the tail call there (afterCall) and run the traced function again from that pc with the recording's tracer active; or have the recompiler emit a self `jal` as a real call.

name: showScore
text: `recorderEntry` then sees `tailPending()` and runs the untraced functions from pc until pc equals the outer's return address: showScore returns to ra 0x1B4DFC (the self-call's return), so the loop runs the resumable entry at 0x1B4DFC (the rest of the outer, untraced: the flags test and its own tail call to showScore, a direct C++ call) to the real return.

text: 1. **Record** real calls in the game: `PS2X_FNREC=<names or addresses, or all> PS2X_FNREC_DIR=/tmp/...`. The registered functions are built a second time from `recomp/generated` with every load, store and call traced (`fncheck_traced.h`: the generated code is unchanged, only the macros it is written in). A recorded call keeps: the registers at entry and at the return; every byte it read, as it was at entry; every byte it or its callees wrote, as it is at the return (the dead stack below sp left out); and each call it made: target, arguments, the registers it returned with and what it changed in RAM (a full RAM diff around the call); and the EE cycles its own code charged.

name: setSkaterScore
text: A function that calls itself is followed through the inner call: generated code makes the self-call a jump to the function's start with ra at the return point, so the inner call's return (jr ra, or the jump of its tail call) leaves the C++ function there; the recorder ends the inner call's tail call at that point (the jal to the function itself two words before it) and goes on with the outer call there, traced, and ps2xFnCheck's replay of the original does the same (round 10; setSkaterScore's rollover).

name: setSkaterScore
text: A long function (many calls) is unwound at an EE safe point in most of its calls, which are then not kept: `PS2X_FNREC_ATOMIC=1` runs each recorded call with safe points held off (a host-made guest call, callees that leave by a jump run on to their return), as a readable version runs in the game; the report says why calls were not kept. Record with `PS2X_READABLE=off`. Recordings are game data: they stay in a scratch folder (`[workshop file]`, not /tmp, which macOS clears at a restart), never in a repository.

A fix: when the tail-pending loop reaches an address inside the recorded function itself (a resumable entry), close the tail call there (afterCall) and run the traced function again from that pc with the recording's tracer active; or have the recompiler emit a self `jal` as a real call.

text: Its cause is the original's call of itself (the dereference "*name": the variable's text followed as a path): generated code compiles that jal to a jump to its own start, so the inner return, a jr to 0x185CE4, leaves the C++ function and comes back through the scheduler, and every caller up the chain returns through it too (zgehand5's checkFaceTree case). resolvePath and setSkaterScore (its rollover call of itself) now make that call through `ee::selfCall` (ee/abi.h, drafter18). ps2xFnCheck replays such a return in place, which is why `--safepoints` never showed it.

text: It runs inside the game's pause (mode 3): the pause update 0x1BC280 is replaced by a free camera that writes the player camera 0x24C9D0 (+0x10 eye, +0x20 look-at point, +0x30 FOV) in camera mode 5 (look-at); roll by turning the rows of the look-at matrix 0x13A260 (which ignores its roll argument). text: It opens a DMA CALL tag (FUN_001D8740, identical to AI's FUN_00210D78) to the table's chain (+8 / +0xC); the payload is the VIF state once a frame (STROW 1.0, BASE, OFFSET 0x200: double buffers of 0x200 qwords, AI 0x1E0), the texture request (MARK, an interrupt-bit MSKPATH3), the world matrix (node +0x50, UNPACK V4-32 at TOPS), and MSCAL type, or type + 2 with one more qword (the camera's near plane in object space, w 1.25) when (cullFlags & 0x22) == 2, or 0x1A for type 4 when (cullFlags & 0xC) == 0, then MSCAL 0.

The app gives zgui's heap 64 KB more when the pages are on (aggressive_inline_settings_room.cpp).

name: answerSaveMenuFromVariable
text: - **Passthrough with arguments of its own** (passthrough_args widened): FUN_0017FD00 reads a0 and hands a0 and a1 on to its `jalr`; FUN_001DE208 sets a1 to its frame (an out pointer) before calling it, and its draft passed only a0, so the callee wrote through FUN_001DE208's caller's a1 and the draft read its own frame word unset. A function that hands an entry argument register on to an indirect or variadic call is now variadic for its callers even when it reads some arguments itself (they pass what they set; a register they leave is their caller's, still in the context).

name: updateSoundEmitters

No route's level has a repeating emitter (the three uncovered blocks). name: scriptMessageHandler
text: Events are engine messages: entering a state subscribes the script object handler FUN_001DF480 to the state's events on the scene object of the same name and sends it "enter"; a message runs the handler (FUN_001E0600) with its data pushed (the get*Data natives read it). SEND and SET keep ip and frame on the stack, since the handlers they run nest. Engine message 0x7000 is never reported handled.

name: scriptMessageHandler
text: So 13 of the level's 41 lesson props (instances named *_L<n>) stayed on in every lesson and in free skate: lessons 19 and 24's quarter pipes stand in the same two places (Scriptobj_qpipe_1_L19 and _1_L24 at -2.3, 1.8; _2_L19 and _2_L24 at 11.4, -6.4), drawn over each other: the flashing green and wooden ramp. ps2xGcConvert lists TUT.BIN's 42 calls for the objects TUTT.BIN never shows or hides, for the objects and states TUTT.BIN has (VISIBILITY.TXT); the override makes them after each such enter (the engine message handler func_1DF480 wrapped, so the level start's first enters as well as func_1E0798's switches), as the native does (nativeSetObjectVisible: the node and its collision, keep 1).

Its callers are the TrafficLight level object's newTrafficLight (the first path segment found), its frame message's updateTrafficLight and trafficLightSegmentsClear; AI never registers that object type (registerTrafficLightType: no caller or pointer in SLUS_203.27) and no AI level has a TrafficLight object (the PS2 and Xbox images name only Prop_TrafficLightA..C props and TrafficLightsCam; the bare type name occurs once, in the ELF). Reaching it needs DM2's traffic lights brought into AI's level format with their paths, then the type registered by AI's level setup: a level-conversion task, not a play goal.

- VIF1/VU1 (with the GIF arbiter and PATH3) run on a worker thread, GS packet processing on a second one (`PS2X_VU1_ASYNC=0` turns it off). The EE sees the same state as before: DMA completion at kick time as before; interrupt-bit VIFcodes (the game's VIF1 handler runs once or twice per frame) are found by a framing scan of each stream on the EE, which also keeps a shadow of the VIF1 registers so the handler's STAT/MARK/CODE and GIF_STAT reads do not wait (`PS2X_VIF1_SHADOW_CHECK=1` verifies it); VU1 memory, GS privileged registers and GS HLE calls drain the workers. The double-buffer swap (sceGsSwapDBuffDc) is queued behind the frame's GS work, at most one frame ahead.

- The live-play profile (2026-10-24; [workshop file]: per level fnprof.csv, route.out, mash logs; merged.csv): `style=natural`, seed 7, readable off, unpaced, the null GS and VU1 skipped (so sceGsSwapDBuffDc, the EE waiting for the GS, is 0.2 s: left out of the totals anyway), PS2X_FNPROF_FROM 120 vsyncs after the skater was placed (a dry run found the vsync), PS2X_FNPROF_FOR 10,800, one run at a time (peak 300 MB):

`PS2X_PAD_PORT1=mirror` keeps the old routing for developer runs that drive split screen with one input (tools/loadtime.py sets it; routes.py `splitscreen` and speedsweep.py `mp` need it, DEVTOOLS.md).

**Fix (runtime, Pad.cpp, ps2_pad.cpp, ps2_host_input):** port 1 has a pad only while player 2's own gamepad is connected (`PortSource.connected`, `PSPadBackend::portConnected`); without one it is an empty port: scePadGetState DISCONNECTED, scePadRead returns 0 with nothing pressed (libpad's failed read), the info and setup calls (InfoMode, InfoAct, InfoPressMode, SetMainMode, Enter/ExitPressMode, SetActAlign, SetActDirect) fail; a pad that goes away loses its mode and motors, so the game redoes its setup when one comes back, as with a real pad. The pad script, the control channel and override presses are player 1's (port 0).

1. *DM2 level records written on the EE every 10 s.* While a DM2 level is played in AI, aggressive_inline_dm2level.cpp's syncRecords (a VSync hook) wrote the records file with writeFileAtomic (temp file, flush to disk, backup, rename) whenever the row had changed, which it does during play: every 10 s. On [workshop machine] the write took 50-167 ms on the EE (traced; game frames of 66-184 ms, "pacer dropped ... ms of catch-up" after every "[dm2level] records of WOODWARD saved"); on the Mac a few ms. Now `ps2x::saves::writeFileAtomicLater`: one background writer (requests in order, the newest data per file wins, drained at exit and before readWithBackup).

After the run the game sets the cursor back to Woodward.

**The slot:** DM2's per-level tables (stats at 0x215BA0 + level * 0x21C, far clips 0x21CC70, goals, gaps) have rows for its eight levels and the park editor only, so the Movie Lot runs in Woodward Camp's (level 2, never locked). `dave_mirra_ailevel.cpp` (PS2X_AI_LEVELS_DIR): a UILIB.ZAL patch gives MainMenu.SelectLevel value 9 in Free Ride (MaxValue + 2, name and text in SetupStats, no picture); the menu-to-level table 0x25A1C8 gets 9 -> 2 in its unused byte; while Root.CurrentLevel is 9 the Woodward folder's ZIT is the Movie Lot's (which names MOVIE.GEO/INS/TXR/DAT, served from the folder) and Woodward's far-clip entry reads 0 (so the level's Globals far clip is used).

**Each AI level its own records.** DM2's level records (0x21C bytes per level at 0x215A88, 13 records of 0x14: value, rider, name; FUN_00165C78; part of the game save) had Woodward's row for all seven.

In Dave Mirra BMX 2 the same setting (or `PS2X_DM2_OPEN_LEVELS=1`) opens every level in the level select (dave_mirra_devlevels.cpp, PS2Recomp `rider5`): each vsync it sets bit 0 ("open") of the progress flags of each of DM2's eight levels for every rider (0x2174B4 + rider x 0x3C8 + 0x13C + level x 0x44 + 0x3C), which bmxSetupLevelStats (0x1AFE58) reads before it locks a level. The Xbox levels' career keeps its own (dave_mirra_xcareer.cpp). Pad scripts then reach any level with RIGHT presses at the level select (menu value v: v presses; level ids by value 2, 1, 0, 3, 6, 5, 4, 7). Off by default.

libkernel's fio calls (sceIoctl2 0x2196D8, sceFormat 0x219C50 and the rest) build one request at 0x2ADFC4: +0 the address of the reply word (a stack slot), +4 its size (always 4), +8 (0x2ADFCC) the payload: a 0x400-byte path (ended by a store to 0x2AE3CB) or words, a second path at 0x2AE3CC, a third field at 0x2AE7CC, then the call's arglen / bufp / buflen words at the end of the last path (sceIoctl2 0x2AE3D4 bufp, 0x2AE3D8 buflen, 0x2AE3DC arglen; sceDevctl 0x2AE7CC cmd, 0x2AE7D0 arglen).

**IOP.** With native disc, movies and sound every IRX the game loads is skipped (SIO2MAN, PADMAN, MCMAN, MCSERV, LIBSD, SDRDRV, ZAUDIO, ZCDDVD), so the game override stops the IOP altogether (`PS2Runtime::setIopStopped`): no R3000 interpreter, no IOP clock, no SPU2 mixing; its memory and heap remain for the EE's bookkeeping calls (sceSifAllocIopHeap etc.). `PS2X_IOP=1` runs it anyway; with any of `PS2X_DISC=cdvd`, `PS2X_MOVIES=hle`, `PS2X_SOUND=spu2` the modules load and it runs.

InitTLBFunctions (libkernl) installs the TLB syscall handlers: SetSyscall(0x21D378) with the pairs at 0x2613B0..0x2613C4, a kernel copy of 808 bytes from 0x261040 to [address] (0x21D320), FlushCache(0) and (2), then for syscalls 4-8 GetEntryAddress (RFU091 0x21D368, a0 from the table at 0x2613C8) and SetSyscall with its result; every callee is a raw syscall wrapper reading its arguments from a0-a3.

In the runtime, syscall 0x5B after InitTLBFunctions' SetSyscall(0x5B, [address]) answers KE_ERROR (dispatchSyscallOverride: no recompiled function at the copied TLB code), so the loop installs 0xFFFFFFFF for syscalls 0x55..0x59 (the TLB functions: SetTLBEntry and InitTLB32MB call 0x56) and later calls of them answer KE_ERROR; on a PS2 they are the TLB code's entries. Harmless while nothing reaches the TLB functions (the runtime's memory is flat); seen in AI's and BMX XXX's recordings (a1 = -1).

**Recording across a wait.** A call that waits (sceMcSync, a semaphore; a tail call to one too) is parked: its open call's RAM image made whole, the return point's table slot taken; when its thread comes back there with that sp the call ends and the function is traced on to its return. cov-autoload's card functions: 18 functions and 410 calls kept before, 28 and 781 now, every call replaying identically. `PS2X_FNREC_WAITS=0` drops them as before. callGuestFunction and the atomic recorder now restore their state when a wait throws through them (callGuestFunction's guest-call depth stayed raised).

- **Calls that wait are dropped without a count.** The card code (Options > Save & Load, the pause SAVE, the boot autoload, the card dialogs) runs on these routes (the card's files are written) but of the 90 "memory card" functions 21 are entered through the recorder on these routes and 1 is kept: a call that waits (sceMcSync, a semaphore) throws to the scheduler, recorderEntry's Scope unwinds, and the exit line says "0 calls recorded of 11 (0 not kept: yielded ...)". The other 69 did not enter it on these routes (paths2's park save and load reached 16). Recording across a wait (or an FNCYCLES identity check) is what the card code, the boot init and the level exit need.

__udivdi3's first port was a plain d != 0 ? n / d : ~0 and passed every recorded call (8,812; 28 of 79 blocks): no recording divides by zero. In AI's A/B at clock 4096 it alone zeroed the profiler's cycle tables (0x23F2B8-0x23F3E8) from the first dump of frontend, messages and editor: the game divides by a zero elapsed time, where libgcc2.c's __udivmoddi4 does its deliberate 1 / d0, the R5900's divu leaves LO = 0xFFFFFFFF (no trap; the recompiled divu agrees) and the division runs on with d0 = 0xFFFFFFFF. Since 2f050dcbc the body is GCC 2.95.2's __udivmoddi4 with longlong.h's C fallbacks; __umoddi3 and __divdi3 go through it; the library suite holds 900 operand pairs with zero divisors, identical to the original.

__udivdi3 stays Tested after the port (cov4 g4b, runner 00d752379, clock 4096): on alone with the defaults, frontend, messages and editor still differ from off in the same RAM words as before the port (0x23F318-0x23F408, 0x30-byte records: a count growing ~8 a tick, a flag 1, and 64-bit sign-extended cycle counts like 0xFFFFFFFF927C0000 that off stores and on leaves 0; copies on the heap 0x970AE0 and the main stack 0x1EFFF18). Its arithmetic is proven (900 suite pairs identical to the original, zero divisors included, and the late recordings), so the difference is in how the game sees the call, not the quotient: for a code lane with a differential trace. Its original callers: timeMilliseconds, _strtol_r, _strtoul_r, _vfprintf_r, _vfiprintf_r and five unregistered libc internals (0x2165f8, 0x2251e4, 0x225d50, 0x22c7d0, 0x22d2f8).

The bracket runs (cov4 gate/trace: frontend to 3100, off and on,__udivdi3, PS2X_FNCYCLES over __udivdi3 and its callers, PS2X_FNCYCLES_WATCH on the words): the differing words are the save-job thread's stack (thread 6, 0x23E490+0x1000, sp 0x23F330 at t3000: live frames above it), the frames of waitMilliseconds -> timeMilliseconds -> __udivdi3 (zge/platform/memory_card.cpp, zge/debug/cycle_counter.cpp): off and the defaults leave the original's temporaries there (0x2010, 1, the ms quotients, sign-extended COUNT values); with __udivdi3 readable the readable chain calls it directly (enterFrame with its 0x10 frame row, no saves) and the caller's frame words come out 0 or elsewhere. So the runtime's direct-call frame model for a readable leaf under readable callers, not the quotient: abi.cpp (enterFrame, calleeSp, ee::Local placement) is the place; the same exposure for any readable leaf with a frame row and no saves called directly from readable code.

__udivdi3 stays Tested (frame1): the A/B difference cov4 found with it readable is not its quotient or its frame (every call has the original's sp, 0x23F320 under timeMilliseconds) but the caller-saved registers it leaves. Other threads' writes fault the same way; a file read straight into RAM (a large `fread` reads with the system call, which fails on a read-only page) says so first (`runtime/ps2_host_write.h`, called by the three readers that read into guest memory). The scratchpad and RAM's bytes outside whole pages are still copied and compared. `PS2X_FNREC_EFFECTS=diff` keeps the full RAM diff (the reference).

- **Callee writes by page protection.** Around each call a recorded function makes, EE RAM is made read-only (one `mprotect` / `VirtualProtect`), the first write to a page faults, the handler (SIGBUS/SIGSEGV, or a vectored handler on Windows) copies the page and makes it writable, and at the return only the copied pages are compared. Nested calls (a recorded callee's own callees) keep an interval each; a page's copy serves every open interval that had not seen it.

The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: ps2SifInit
text: ps2SifInit's module loaders (zge/platform/boot.cpp, shared by the three games) returned the failing module's name as their failure, 0 meaning none, so a module whose name word is 0 and whose load failed read as loaded (sceSifInitIopHeap, OK, 1), where the original decides on sceSifLoadModule's v0 < 0 and reports the module. Found by cov5's differential cases (BMX, a null host path word: 14 of 175 differed); fixed in cov5's dded27ea1: the loaders return whether every module loaded and give the failing name apart. After the fix the 175 cases are identical, and the corpus replays (AI 19, DM2 66, BMX 33 files), lc 21/21 and dm2logic 6/6 pass.

name: loadCollisionTreeChunk
text: DM2's TGCI on disc: {u32 part id, u32 bytes, the tree}, the nodes in preorder with the greater side first, each split 8 bytes (axis, a byte, s16 plane in hundredths, u16 word offsets of the greater and lesser child) and each leaf inline (0, a byte, u16 count, the u16 faces), padded to 4 bytes; nothing after the tree. Byte +1 of every node and the two bytes after an odd leaf's faces are exporter leftovers (not zero in 119,604 splits and about 18,000 leaves): Woodward rewritten with them all 0 ran dm2logic 6/6 MATCH as the stock files. Every DM2 tree lists exactly its part's faces with 0x2000 (945,970, none left out, none extra), unlike AI's. dm2_level_write.py InlineCollisionTree.

name: loadCollisionTreeChunk
text: A DM2 collision tree's partition is part of the physics: Woodward with its 260 trees rebuilt by a median-split builder over exactly the stock trees' faces (dm2_level_write.py rewrite --rebuild-trees) diverged from the reference at dm2logic's ck4-ride-turn (0.018 m, 1.15 m by ck6), while the writers' copy with the stock trees matched 6/6. As in AI (zge3w): a stock level keeps its trees; a level of our own gets a built tree as its own behaviour.

First at call #104: sp-0xb0 (EE 0x01effca0) holds 0x410a0000 where the original leaves 0x00000000 (byte 2, which the original writes in the call), read by forEachSelectedCell (0x1B6620) at its call #640, vsync 7010; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. name: readHmtlChunk
text: DM2's readHmtlChunk builds its flag word on s3 as the dispatching loop left it: readHfntChunk's font page loop keeps kNoMoreChunks (-1) there, parseChunks its done flag, readHlibChunk its result's address. The readable tells the font page by the texture callback readHfntChunk set (addLoadedTextureToMaterial), since the readable font loop keeps nothing in s3 (before 5a37d1e12 the front end's five font assets got 0x111 for 0xFFFFF111).

name: readHmtlChunk

The flag word it stores at +0xB0 of its record keeps the caller's s3 above the chunk's low 12 bits (fr-trainyards tick 1: 0xFFFFF111 in the original's register model, 0x111 with the held-register table off). BMX XXX's counterpart does the same (0x006BD111 vs 0x111).

name: readHmtlChunk
text: readHmtlChunk (DM2's readHmtlChunks) takes the flag word above its 12 bits from the register its dispatching loop left (the kept bug). Guessing that word from the texture callback (kNoMoreChunks when the callback it replaces is addLoadedTextureToMaterial, verify1's 5a37d1e12) is wrong: the callback stays set after a font load, so the editor's library loads (readHlibChunk's loop, word 0x0015C000) got 0xFFFFF110 for the original's 0x0015C110 (int15's replay, 4 recordings: ed-card, editor-0/1/2). Reverted in int15's 8700af711; Tested until the caller's held register reaches it (tools18).

name: readHfntChunk

name: levelStateEnter
text: The PS2 disc's REPLAY.ZAL (48 one-asset groups, 16 on the NPCs') holds real demo replays only in groups 6 and 7 (level 3: Rider00, 5479 frames; Rider01, 66016 bytes, past levelStateEnter's 0x3800-byte replay); groups 0-5 and 8-15 are left-over bytes (level byte 0, MSVC 0xCD fill) and a demo of them crashes the level (memory written over 16 frames in). The Xbox's replay.zal (60 groups) holds demos of levels 0-4, 6 and 7 (groups 1-4, 6, 7, 9, 13-15), which play on the PS2 to their recorded frame counts. Also: the PS2's boot main menu is the intro state, whose exit keeps the menu scene, so a level entered from it fails enterScene (g_currentScene set).

name: uiFrameFileKind

name: setUiFrame
text: setUiFrame(on, kind, request): the memory card frame (CommonUI.FrameMemCard) turned on or off. Kinds (byte 0x25BAA8): 0 save game, 1 save replay, 2 load game, 3 load replay, 4 the intro's card check, 5 save park, 6 load park, 7 the intro's end. The request is 4 words copied to 0x25BAB8: +0 callback when the frame closes without the work done, +4 data, +8 the data's handle (the editor's park save only), +0xC callback when the work is done; both are called (data, handle). The step byte is 0x25BAB0 (0xFF none; 0x167238 sets it and shows its message).

name: setUiFrame
text: The frame kind 7 is the auto load, not 'the intro's end': its title is KSTR_SAVE_TITLE07 'AUTO LOAD' (0 SAVE GAME, 1 SAVE REPLAY, 2 LOAD GAME, 3 LOAD REPLAY, 5 SAVE PARK, 6 LOAD PARK; 4, the start check, has none). It checks card 0 then card 1 and loads the game from the first that has one.

name: uiFrameUpdate
text: uiFrameUpdate(): the memory card frame's run, called by the game states' frames. At a card step (12, 13, 14, 15, 23, 24: 60 frames each, formatting 120) it selects the port at frame 1 (0x17C9E8), starts the card work at frame 10 with the call block 0x25BAC8 (callback uiFrameCardDone, argument 0x2BAD60), fills the progress bar (300 wide) until the step's frames are up, then reads the result at 0x2569D0 (-1 working, 0 done, 1 no card, 3 changed, 4 removed, 5 unformatted, 6 no file, 7 file there, 8 no space, else failed) and picks the next step. 0x256B38 is the work started: 0 check 0x17CDE8, 1 create 0x17CC58, 2 format 0x17D0A0, 3 load 0x17D198, 4 save 0x17D350, 5 free-space check 0x17D000, 6 file look-up 0x17CF18. Always 0.

First at call #0: sp-0x150 (EE 0x01effae0) holds [address] where the original leaves 0x00000001 (byte 2, which the original writes in the call), read by resolveBodyContacts (0x13FB80) at its call #608, vsync 13139; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: playerSpawnPoint
text: DM2 PS2 0x001910E0 playerSpawnPoint: reachable, no recording yet (it stays Draft). Input: MULTIPLAYER, two riders and bikes, level Woodward (or Devils' Peak), game RANDOM SPOT (kind 4; dm2routes.py multiplayer(3, level): DOWN x3 on SELECT GAME), and play round after round: each round's first player draws one spot. A draw nearest a sunk Player locator calls it; that is 286 of the 65,536 possible draws on Woodward (0.44%), 414 on Devils' Peak (0.63%), 88 on Trainyards (0.13%), e.g. Woodward x byte 125, z byte 137, so a recording must play many rounds (or games) until one lands; the randomNumber sequence decides which Not recorded: a draw lands on such a locator in under 1 % of rounds, which a fixed route cannot aim for. Why: Only caller spawnAtPlayer (0x191AB8, rider/physics/respawn.cpp:271) at 0x191D18 (block 0 hits), when the spiral gave no face (or flags bit 0 skipped it) and locatorMatrix's nearest Spawn/Player locator gave no face (no ground under it, a down-facing hit, or an object: hit->face 0). Random Spot (kRandomSpawnMode 4, game/round.cpp:723-735) calls respawnAtStart(place, kDrawnPlaceFlags = 3) with place = (drawBetween(min x, max x), 0, drawBetween(min z, max z)) (256 x 256 possible values, round.cpp:561), so the spiral is skipped and the nearest Player locator to the draw decides. Every level's DAT has many Spawn/Player SDPT points (Woodward 153, Devils' Peak 212, Trainyards 112), and some lie under the floor: with groundBelow's ray from 2 above the point down (rider/contact.cpp:112) over dm2_level.collision_triangles, Woodward (102.0,3.3,103.3) and (47.4,3.3,116.0), Devils' Peak (23.7,6.9,29.6), (-112.2,2.2,-4.9), (-133.7,-1.5,35.3) and Trainyards (96.2,14.1,152.2) have no collidable up face below (their floor is 2.5..26 units above). The corpus' one Random Spot draw (mp-randomspot) and 15 other locator fallbacks all found ground (blocks 0x191CC8/0x191CE8: 16 hits). The same branch is also reached by a water bail whose spiral fails with such a locator nearest. Geometry from the disc tool, not yet played: the first recording should confirm.

The NPC set-up 0x17DB40 (it names its riders with the string "NPC") sets bits 0 and 1. So rider flag bit 0 means an NPC rider (readable kFlagNpc): touchObject skips the game's touch handler, grindAfter the rumble, bailEnter/bailMove the hands, riderFrame and respawn the bail body, and the camera is left alone.

name: freeRider
text: Frees a rider record (callers: the level's exit 0x163968, physicsShutdown 0x1A2470, game.c 0x17DB40 and 0x17DF28): unless flags bit 0, the bail body's velocity words (+0xE0 .. +0xE8) reset, flags bit 31 cleared, the two contacts removed, the body's three sweep boxes unlinked and freed to the sweep's end pool, its half extents and sweep entry freed; then stopRollSound(rollingVoice), the bike and rider mirrors freed, the bike and rider models released, the rider's scene object deleted when its character (g_playerSetups[player] +3) - 0x11 < 4, the record freed and g_riders[index] cleared.

name: freeRider
text: DM2 freeRider cuts the bail body's box out of the level sweep by hand: per axis it sets prev->next of the low end to the high end's next (never the following end's prev), or clears the axis head when the low end is first, then pool-frees both ends. It works because the body is first parked at 10000 on every axis and re-sorted (sweepUpdateBody), so its ends are the last on each list.

name: freeRider
