name: linkNodeFaces
text: The terrain tag callback the level's start sets (0x1AD720: terrainTag(0x1AC498, 0)): for a node, the edges whose tag kind (0x1AD000: tagByte(record, 2, 4) 1 or 2) is set are recorded in 0x70-byte records (0x1AC790: kind, start, end, unit direction, two planes through the edge, the face and edge indices); faces of the same kind with no link word get the edge linked (0x1ACD70, via 0x1ACD28 writing (handle & 0xFFFFFF | side << 24) at record +4; 0x1ACD48 writes -1), the others the nearest edge record of their kind within 16 (0x1ACDE8) by their centroid (0x1AC928, 0x1ACB88 the facing test, 0x1ACC98 all vertices in front of the planes).

name: linkNodeFaces
text: linkNodeFaces with taggedFaceVisitor (0x1AC2F8) and collectFace (0x17A780, 703k calls) take about 0.9 s of a DM2 level load on the Mac (FNPROF over the user's Woodward load, vsyncs 2058-2103: 430 + 386 + 111 ms self of 2.2 s), the largest part after the animation files' AROT keys.

name: fillLinkEdge
text: The linker's edge record (0x70): +0 the side's tag record, +0x10 start, +0x20 end, +0x30 unit direction, +0x40 the upright plane through the edge (normal unit((0,-1,0) x direction)), +0x50 the plane with normal (that normal x direction), +0x60 face, +0x64 side.

name: tagGrindable
text: DM2's tag accessors read TGFE edge records at byte 5 (bit 0 grindable), 6 (grind side 0..3), 7 (wall kind 0..15) and TGFT face records at word 0 (tag), word 4 (link: face 24 bits, side top byte, ~0 none), byte 8 (surface kind), byte 9 (a jump lip's launch strength). tagByte's/tagWord's second argument (2, 8) is unused.

name: globalsLightColour
text: The level's scene point Globals (findScenePoint(nameHash("Globals"), 0, 0); ZGE2's scene point keeps its tag record at +0x10): colour words (group 0x20) 0 the scene light's colour (newSceneLight in the camera set-up 0x168378), 4 the clear colour, 8 the fog colour; floats (group 8) 0xC the fog start, 0x10 the far clip (defaulted and held to 11 or more by the camera set-up). One reader each: 0x1AD280, 0x1AD2E0, 0x1AD340, 0x1AD3A0, 0x1AD400. AI reads the same point in camera.cpp with ZGE3's offsets.

Each base's DAT has exactly one SDPT chunk with kind name_hash("Spawn") and name name_hash("PlayerOne") (scanned with dm2_level.parse/walk, SdptChunk +4/+8: engine/zge/scene/locators.h:55), so the point is always found and only moved, never added. No other code adds a Spawn point.

name: bmxmenuGameMovieUpdate
text: bmxmenuGameMovieUpdate formats 15 gallery rows (Intro and the 14 riders) on the PS2; UILIB's static list has a 16th, !Retro, and the ELF names assets\movie\retro.pss, which the PS2 disc lacks. The GameCube ([address]) and Xbox ([address]) counterparts format 16 rows and open Retro on g_openFeatures bit 3 (KSTRSP_REWARD_FEATURE03, given by the GameCube's last respect reward); the retro movie ships only there (Xbox retro.bik 108.9 s, GC retro.h4m).

name: bmxmenuGameMovieUpdate

name: loadPark
text: The park stream in BMX2PARK.DAT (parks at 0x1130 + slot x 0x2565) is read in this order: version (4, 0x100), theme (1), start (column, row, turns, placed), then each cell by row: level, has-object (then object, a dropped byte, rotation, column, row), rails (has-rails, then group, slots, and type and slot per set bit).

name: loadPark
text: loadPark reads the park stream with no length check: version and start (9 bytes), 3 bytes per empty cell, then the gaps header (7), the scores (0x21C) and the brightness (4); the buffer is kParkBytes (0x2565), so a theme of 64 x 64 cells (12,297 bytes for an empty park) runs past it, reads an object where there is none and newPlacedObject's cell loop never ends; 56 x 56 and 48 x 48 load (dm2_level_convert.py park_fits).

name: savePark
text: DM2 park stream: u32 version 0x100, u8 theme, the view (0x1C4198), per cell by row then column: u8 level, u8 has-object (+ the object 0x1BB0C0) and the cell's rails (0x1BC698; a covered cell that is not the object's own writes two zero bytes), the gaps (0x1C2EF0), the scores, u32 brightness

name: drawHeldObjectBox
text: DM2 drawHeldObjectBox (0x1B8DC0) leaves its own frame unlike the original at its return, where a later function reads it unset and acts on it: in 218 of 292 recorded calls (0 of them reading a nonzero byte of the word) a byte below its entry sp differs from what the original leaves. First at call #0: sp-0x144 (EE 0x01effdec) holds 0x423a05e7 where the original leaves 0x408ffc00 (byte 0, which the original writes in the call), read by drawSkinned (0x1099E0) at its call #1, vsync 11037; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: fitCellTower

So a custom level served in the park slot takes a stock theme's place: its files at that theme's folder, its block in THEMES.TXT replaced (dm2_level_convert.py). name: chooseJunctionExit
text: chooseJunctionExit(object, words, offset): weights a, b, c are floats at offset, +4, +8 of the object's component; the random word at +0xC is drawn on (multiplier 1588635695 mod 2^32-5 by Schrage, q 2, r 1117695901) and written back. Shares are a*100/sum^2 and c*100/sum^2 (fractions when the weights are percents summing to 100; all about 0 gives 33.3 of 99.9 each); draw = u/(2^32-5) + 1e-5: exit 0 up to a's share, 1 up to a's + c's, else 2.

name: buildTextureUploadPacket
text: ZGE4 buildTextureUploadPacket: an image without alpha (flags bit 0) drops the texture's first level when its second arrives, with g_dropLargeTextureLevels set and the base 64 or more wide (levelCount 0, freeIn(level 0's texels, 3), the base size and log2s again): so the texture keeps its levels from the first under 64 wide. A 32-bit picture's texels are copied word by word with each alpha byte halved, where ZGE3 calls memoryCopy. Written (kIsBmx steps).

ZGE4 texture settings at gp+0x115C and gp+0x1160 (setter 0x106F08: option 1, 2). +0x1160: the last mip level a texture may have (initGsTextures: 3, 1 in PAL; buildGsTextureUpload 0x106D88 has room while levelCount <= it, where ZGE3 tests g_gsVideoMode == 3). +0x115C (0 at init): buildTextureUploadPacket drops a 64+ wide texture's first level when its second arrives. Not written.

text: ZGE4 has seven memory kinds (BMX allocateIn's jump table [address]): 0 and 5 rounded to 64 and aligned 128, 1 aligned 64, 2 the main region, 3, 4 and 6 aligned 128 unrounded; no caller passes kind 6 directly.

The VU0 microprogram (VCALLMS 0) works all four lanes of vf1: qmtc2 puts all 128 bits of a0 there, so vf1.z is the caller's leftover upper half of a0, MULz.w copies it to w, and the z and w lanes run the cosine polynomial on that leftover; the program leaves vf1..vf6 so. ps2xFnCheck (portbmx3, replay 1117-083057, 98 files, 10031 calls each) finds vf2.w (u^8 of that leftover lane) live after the return in 3170 of angleSin's and 2541 of angleCos' calls: the readable bodies, which give x and y alone, fail there; originals all original_ok.

TGFV (readTgfvChunk, ZGE4 only: loadBufferStreamChunk's TGFE/TGFT form) is a part's corner tags: a tag buffer with one u16 index per face corner (3 x face + corner, the indices padded to 16 with zeros) and 4-byte records. Only the fast cars have them (fastCarDef_*, 14 parts over the eight levels, 163 records): byte 0 is the skitch hold kind (1 or 2: cornerTagKind reads it, cornerKind maps it to kCornerHold / kCornerHoldMirrored), bytes 1-3 vary (44 of 163 not zero) and the corner code reads byte 0 alone. tooling ai/tools/zge_tags.py CornerTag4 reads and writes it; bmx_level_write.py round trips every GEO byte-identically.

The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: bodiesTouch
text: BMX XXX bodiesTouch (0x1A6758) leaves its own frame unlike the original at its return, where a later function reads it unset and acts on it: in 50 of 847 recorded calls (0 of them reading a nonzero byte of the word) a byte below its entry sp differs from what the original leaves. First at call #308: sp-0x21c (EE 0x01fdfbe4) holds 0x0179d3d0 where the original leaves 0x01799200 (byte 0, which the original writes in the call), read by bmx_174440 (0x174440) at its call #832 through its callee, vsync 6074; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: spawnTracer
text: BMX XXX PS2 0x001A7C00 spawnTracer: no input of the shipped game reaches it (it stays Draft). spawnTracer (games/bmx/fx/spawns.cpp:66-79) is the only caller of spawnNamedEffect with nameHash("tracer") 0x059657A2, and its only caller is fireShot 0x1E7560 (games/bmx/weapon/projectiles.cpp:176-186, block 0x1E76CC), which calls it only for a weapon with kWeaponTracers 0x40 when shooter->ammunition[weapon].loaded (lhu 0x8(shooter+weapon*4) at 0x1E76B4) has (loaded & 3) == 0 or loaded < 6. The weapon table 0x292280 (read-only: no store into it in its four readers) gives that flag only to weapon 3 (flags 0x42 = repeats|tracers, clip 50, reserve 150; weapon 1 is the scoped one, flags 0x28). loaded is written only by resetShooter (= clip, games/bmx/weapon/weapons.cpp:419) and the kShooterLoading step (+= min(clip - loaded, reserve), weapons.cpp:255-257, which adds 0 to a full clip); nothing ever lowers it: no decrement in updateShooter 0x1E6B08 (its kShooterFiring case 0x1E7198 calls fireShot, weaponSound, beginState only), fireShot or the projectile owners (riderProjectileEvent 0x1E5F88, riderHitByProjectile 0x1DAAC0, riderHitAllowed 0x1AFDD0, playerWeaponProjectileEvent 0x1EA6C8 have no sh), and a scan of all generated code finds no lhu/addiu -1/sh of a halfword outside the pool helpers and two unrelated functions. So weapon 3 always fires with loaded = 50 (50 & 3 = 2, 50 >= 6) and the tracer branch is dead. The corpus agrees: int40 fireShot ran block 0x1E76AC (tracer weapon) 3 times in mp1 and 9 in mp3-pb, and 0x1E76CC never, which a falling count could not give over 9 shots by two players. The earlier routes1 note (mp-paintball-snipe, "sniper weapon 3") assumed the count falls and that weapon 3 is the scope weapon; both are contradicted by the code above. initEffects (games/bmx/fx/library.cpp:163-174, BMX 0x1A7228) registers each starter only as a named class (registerNamedEffectClass 0x174B28); that registry g_namedEffectClasses [address] is read only by 0x174B28, initEffectTables 0x174608, freeNamedEffectClasses 0x174658 and spawnNamedEffect(ByWalk) 0x174B90 (func_globals), no data word or code address-build holds 0x174B90, and all seven callers of 0x174B90 load a constant hash into a0 just before the jal: grindSparks 0x1A7B50 spark 0x0058466B, spawnTracer 0x1A7C00 tracer 0x059657A2, debris 0x1A7F58 and spawnShardFromTriangle 0x1A8738 shard 0x0057C664 / screenshard 0x0A6040F4, spawnSkidMark 0x1A8370 skid 0x00057FD4, spawnBulletMark 0x1A8530 pockmark 0x0380133B, sleep 0x1A86F8 sleep 0x005809A0 (generated-ns lui/ori). The class records (spark 0x283ED0, tracer 0x283F08, splash 0x283FB0, dust 0x283FE8, ripple 0x284058, lightning 0x284090) are referenced only by initEffects and shutdownEffects 0x1A76A8 (func_globals), and findEffectClassByName 0x174940 and startEffect 0x159108 are called only from startNamedEffect 0x159260, whose callers are the class starters and startWaterWake 0x209440 (class "WaterWake" only, games/bmx/level/water_wake.cpp:225-240); no data word holds 0x159260, 0x159108 or 0x174940.

name: spawnShards
text: spawnShards: when the effects' particle budget is used up no shard is allocated, and BMX XXX still writes the shard's fields at address 0 and adds 0 to the emitter's array (Aggressive Inline breaks out of the loop instead).

name: spawnShards
text: BMX XXX spawnShards (0x1AA1F0) leaves its own frame unlike the original at its return, where a later function reads it unset and acts on it: in 8 of 605 recorded calls (0 of them reading a nonzero byte of the word) a byte below its entry sp differs from what the original leaves. First at call #1: sp-0xac (EE 0x01fdf824) holds 0xbeb340fd where the original leaves 0x0000172d (byte 2, which the original writes in the call), read by closestOnRail (0x1D42E8) at its call #7, vsync 7914; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The word read there is zeros in the original, which another write may leave as well. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

name: drawShards

name: gameMode
text: gameMode: the byte 0x29EC57, an index of the 0x14-byte mode records at 0x284300 (rounds +0, flags +4 with 0x2 for a multiplayer mode, a float +8); mode 1 is the competition (roundCount answers 2, startGame draws its field). DM2's multiplayerMode and singlePlayerMode made one.

name: setRoundPhase
text: BMX setRoundPhase(phase): the round's phase machine, five phases: 1 game start, 2 turn start, 3 turn running, 4 turn over, 5 game over (DM2's 1, 3, 5, 7, 8). The round's state is one record at 0x2F35A0: flags +0 (0x01 game ends, 0x02 round done, 0x04 first turn, 0x08 tie, 0x10 round drawn; 0x20..0x100 BMX's own), the phase's clock in frames +4, the turn-end stage +0xD with its frame count +8, round winners +0x1D4, leader +0x1E3, the HORSE word +0x1E4. Mode record (0x14 bytes at 0x284300): +1 scored, +2 scoring (1 turns' sum, 2 rounds won, 3 best turn), flags +4 (0x2 multiplayer, 0x4 turns, 0x80 winner starts, 0x100 the player after the winner starts), +8 the turn's seconds.

name: scoreLines
text: BMX XXX scoreLines (0x1B32A0) leaves its own frame unlike the original at its return, where a later function reads it unset and acts on it: in 309 of 866 recorded calls (8 of them reading a nonzero byte of the word) a byte below its entry sp differs from what the original leaves. First at call #36: sp-0xb8 (EE 0x01fdfbb8) holds 0x3dbff6e0 where the original leaves 0x00000001 (byte 0, which the original writes in the call), read by airMove (0x1CB548) at its call #44 through its callee, vsync 6586; perturbing the byte changes what that reader does. The replay with the frame-reads index fails these calls (frame_residue_read); without the index the frame is dead stack to the checker and they pass.

Input: Career (challenge) mode, level Dam (CHL_DAM): on the goals list shown before the run (or pause > the goals list), move the cursor DOWN 13 lines to line 13 (Combo15) or 17 lines to RunScoreA (lines from 0 in OBJCTV.TXT order of the IS_CHILD "NO" objectives: Dynamite, Drain, Patch, Brownout, Potty, Canal, Manual, Bungie, Bowling, Roach, Crane, Wallride, BridgeTransfer, Combo15, 5NPCDeliver, Collect30, AllGaps, RunScoreA, RunScoreB, RunScoreC) and press the DETAILS button (the game's pad button bit 0x40, FrameDetails "$KSTR_DETAILS"; zge/input/pads.h calls bit 0x40 kPadCircle, which the controller configuration can move). The detail screen opens and asks the RECORD goal's status. Same in any challenge level (each has Combo* and RunScoreA-C). verdmbx1 tried vr-details-dam (bmxroutes.py: the Dam's pause VIEW CHALLENGES, CIRCLE on each of 26 lines, TRIANGLE back): 5 details opened, none a RECORD goal's (objectivesScreenMessage opens a detail only for a goal that is active or ready to activate), so a RECORD goal has to be taken first. Why: RECORD's statusText hook (games/bmx/objectives/record_type.cpp:68,181-196), referenced only by registerRecordType 0x1F17D0, called through objectiveStatusText 0x16DB08 (engine/zge/scene/objectives.cpp:68-78). Of its callers, objectiveDetailScreenMessage 0x1BA9B8 asks it for g_shownObjective on kScreenEnter (games/bmx/overlay/screen_objectives.cpp:308-330), and objectivesScreenMessage's kScreenButton6 case (screen_objectives.cpp:226-249, sent by games/bmx/ui/menu.cpp:44,163-166 for pad bit 0x40) sets g_shownObjective to the selected line's objective (addObjectiveLine, oldest first: forEachObjective = poolForEachOldestFirst, objectives.cpp:116-122; IS_CHILD objectives have no line) and opens the detail when the goal is marked active (updateGoal sets kGoalActive when it activates, objective_visitors.cpp:300-312) or ready to activate. The disc's RECORD objectives are all IS_CHILD "NO" and active from the start (Combo10..35, RunScoreA-C, GrindDist, Wallride, Record900 in the six CHL_ levels). The other callers do not ask a RECORD: objectiveDisplayFrame/objectiveDisplayMessage show only a timed objective (objective_visitors.cpp:296-312: TIMEOUT), and sendObjectActivatedToObjective only one that took an object's activation. int40: objectiveDetailScreenMessage ran once (p1-dam-gos, 4 messages) on a non-RECORD goal; objectiveStatusText 1382 calls, never a RECORD. name: createAModelLibraryIndex
text: BMX XXX PS2 0x00206928 createAModelLibraryIndex: no input of the shipped game reaches it (it stays Draft). Its only caller is initCreateAModel's default-texture loop (games/bmx/create/create_a_model.cpp:131-142), which runs once per parsed line of assets\create\default.txt. The shipped ASSETS/CREATE/DEFAULT.TXT (828 bytes) has only // comment lines (its example entries are commented out), so the first readStringToken fails and the loop body never runs: in the corpus initCreateAModel ran 39 times with the loop blocks 0x206068/0x206080/0x206098 never hit. Data-dependent: a non-comment line in DEFAULT.TXT would reach it; the disc has none.

The Xbox ([address]) and GameCube ([address]) builds of createAModelGetFilteredListOfAssetsInLibrary pass over a library asset whose name in capitals holds _HUL unless feature 5 (GREEN SKIN) is set (Xbox: SavedGame featuresOn 0x20; GameCube: features 0x20) and one holding _TOPLESS unless feature 6 (TOPLESS GIRL, 0x40); nothing else in either build reads those two bits. The PS2 build has no such test, and its create libraries have no such textures.
